provenance.method: Practical discovery question assembled from reviewed autism-related organisation and resource objects. The synthesis distinguishes support, research and advocacy roles rather than treating all organisations as interchangeable authorities.

question: I want autism information or support. Which kind of organisation am I actually looking for?
why_it_matters: Autism organisations can provide very different things: direct support, information, research, campaigning, peer material or policy advocacy. Treating them as interchangeable can send people to the wrong place or make an advocacy perspective look like neutral clinical authority.
current_understanding: The National Autistic Society is the current catalogue entry most directly oriented toward UK autism information, services, community and directories. Autistica is primarily a research and campaigning charity and explicitly is not a general support service. The Autistic Self Advocacy Network is a US autistic-led disability-rights advocacy organisation, useful for an autistic-led policy perspective rather than as a neutral clinical authority. Autistica Tips Hub contains community-contributed tips and resources; those experiences may be useful but are not universal advice.
evidence_needed: Current first-party scope and access information when organisations change services, geographic reach, leadership or purpose.
A broader reviewed catalogue of local, peer-led and specialist support routes before this question can provide stronger geographic or needs-based navigation.
reopening_conditions: Any listed organisation materially changes its services, geographic scope or organisational role.
New reviewed support organisations or communities materially improve the available routing choices.
dissent: People differ on which organisations they regard as representative, trustworthy or aligned with their values; the catalogue should preserve role and perspective rather than manufacture a single endorsed authority.
